**Symbols:** 84.4% of Apple's iOS API (9176 of 10876, exact) · **Rows:** 128: 110 ✅ 15 🟡 3 ❌ · **iOS:** 2.0+

**Area:** [Foundation & CoreFoundation](../COVERAGE.md#foundation) · **Apple:** [Foundation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation) · **Issues:** [`area:foundation`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Afoundation)

## How isim implements it

- **Adapted:** isim's own Objective-C Foundation (`isim/frameworks/Foundation`) and Swift overlay (`isim/swift/overlays/Foundation`), plus swift-foundation's `Predicate` sources (`FoundationEssentials`).
- **Passthrough** to host libraries:
  - ICU (loaded at run time): locale data;
  - PCRE2: regular expressions;
  - libcurl: `URLSession`;
  - OpenSSL: TLS;
  - inotify: file monitoring.
- iCloud features are simulated locally under `ISIM_DATA`.

| `NSAttributedString` document reading and writing (`init(data:options:documentAttributes:)`, `init(url:options:documentAttributes:)`, `NSMutableAttributedString.read(from:options:documentAttributes:)`, `data(from:documentAttributes:)`, `fileWrapper(from:documentAttributes:)`, `NSAttributedString.DocumentType`, `DocumentAttributeKey`, `DocumentReadingOptionKey`) | ✅ | ≤17 | in isim's UIKit (`NSAttributedStringDocuments.m`; the Objective-C keys and methods are in UIKit's `NSAttributedString.h`, as on iOS). Plain text (the encoding option, else UTF-8 / UTF-16 with a BOM / Windows-1252; Helvetica 12 or the default attributes), RTF (isim's RTF reader) and HTML. HTML is adapted: the host's libxml2 parses it (entities, charset, implied elements) and the elements and CSS map to attributes: Times New Roman 12, headings, bold / italic / underline / strikethrough, colours and backgrounds, links (blue, underlined), alignment, indents, paragraph spacing, lists (markers in the text before iOS 18 or with `textKit1ListMarkerFormatDocumentOption`; drawn by TextKit 2 from the text lists since), line breaks, superscript / subscript, preformatted and monospaced text, tables as tabs, images from file and data URLs. CSS covers inline styles, presentational attributes and `<style>` rules with simple selectors (tag, .class, #id). Not WebKit: no layout of floats or positioning, scripts don't run, remote resources and URLs aren't loaded (only file URLs: `NSFileReadUnsupportedSchemeError`). The type comes from the option, else the URL's extension, else the data. RTF reading also takes links (HYPERLINK fields), backgrounds (`\cb`, `\highlight`), raised text (`\up`, `\dn`) and the page (`\paperw`, `\margl` ..., `\deftab`: `paperSize`, `paperMargin`, `defaultTabInterval`). RTFD: a package (TXT.rtf and its attachments' files, read from a directory URL or a file wrapper's serialized form) whose `{\NeXTGraphic}` attachments become `NSTextAttachment`s with their `fileWrapper` and size. Writing follows Cocoa's writers: RTF (fonts by PostScript name, colours, faces, underline, strikethrough, backgrounds, baseline offset, links as HYPERLINK fields, alignment, indents, spacing, tab stops, Unicode as `\uc0\uN`, the page; attachments dropped), RTFD (`fileWrapper(from:)`: TXT.rtf plus each attachment's file; `data(from:)`: the wrapper's serialized form, isim's own layout), HTML (a `<style>` of `p.pN` / `span.sN` classes, fonts in px as Cocoa writes them, so a round trip reads them back at 3/4 size as on iOS; links; attachments dropped) and plain text in the requested encoding. Tested (HelloHTMLImport, OS matrix; HelloDocumentExport) |

Number agrees with the numeral in the run (French and Portuguese treat 0 ≤ n < 2 as singular) or the explicit morphology: English inflects the head noun, the Romance languages every word up to a preposition, with regular endings and common irregular nouns. Properties (the built-in ones and an app's own `Property` types) are set on a manager; a summary reduces the manager's value and merges its children's, and a finished child's summary is kept through `finalSummary` (file and byte counts add up; a finished child's throughput and time remaining are dropped). A reporter is a read-only view a manager can assign a share to; a `Progress` assigned a share counts its fraction until it finishes (KVO), and a subprogress of a `Progress` starts a manager whose fraction drives a child `Progress` of it. Not observable (`@Observable`) in isim. Tested (HelloMessages: test_messages; HelloDocumentGroup) |

Not provided: icons. Tested (HelloDocumentGroup, HelloDocumentExport) |

### Files, bundles & preferences

| API / feature | Status | iOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| App sandbox container (Documents, Library, Caches, tmp) | ✅ | ≤17 | per app, under `ISIM_DATA` |
| `FileManager` (exists, create, remove, copy, move, list, `urls(for:in:)`, temporary directory) | ✅ | ≤17 | Swift and Objective-C (path and URL forms). `copyItem` copies whole trees (symbolic links as links, permissions and modification dates kept); `moveItem` renames, or copies and removes across file systems; neither replaces an existing item (`NSFileWriteFileExistsError`). Directory enumerators (`enumerator(atPath:)`, `enumerator(at:includingPropertiesForKeys:options:errorHandler:)`, `subpathsOfDirectory(atPath:)`, `contentsOfDirectory(at:includingPropertiesForKeys:options:)`): pre-order, entries sorted by name, links not followed, `skipDescendants`, `level`, `fileAttributes`, the hidden-file / shallow / package / post-order options and the error handler; `NSEnumerator` is a Swift `Sequence`. Symbolic and hard links (`createSymbolicLink`, `destinationOfSymbolicLink`, `linkItem`), `replaceItemAt` / `replaceItem(at:…)` (rename(2), backup item, keeps the original's permissions), `contentsEqual`, `isExecutableFile` / `isDeletableFile`, `currentDirectoryPath` / `changeCurrentDirectoryPath`, file system representation (`NSString.fileSystemRepresentation`, `withFileSystemRepresentation`), `stringByResolvingSymlinksInPath`, the `NSFile*Error` codes (`FoundationErrors.h`). Adapted: packages are directories with a known package extension (`.app`, `.bundle`, `.framework`, …; no Uniform Type lookup); `producesRelativePathURLs` gives absolute URLs; `displayName(atPath:)` is the file name. Tested: FoundationTest, SwiftFoundationTest |
| `for … in` over an `NSEnumerator` / `NSFastEnumeration` (`FileManager.enumerator(atPath:)` and `enumerator(at:…)`, …) in Swift (`NSFastEnumerationIterator`) | ✅ | ≤17 | the objects fast enumeration hands out unretained are not released by the iterator (it used to over-release them, corrupting memory later); tested (HelloFileURLs, `test_file_urls`) |
| URL resource values (`URL.resourceValues(forKeys:)`, `URLResourceKey` / `URLResourceValues`, `setResourceValues`, `-[NSURL resourceValuesForKeys:error:]` / `getResourceValue:forKey:error:` / `setResourceValue(s):…`, temporary and cached values) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: file keys from lstat / access(2) (name, path, parent, file type flags, readable / writable / executable, resource type, (allocated / total) sizes, link count, file and resource identifiers, all dates); `contentType` / `typeIdentifier` / `localizedTypeDescription` through UniformTypeIdentifiers (a built-in table when it is not linked); volume keys from the host's file system (one APFS-like volume "Data": capacities incl. important / opportunistic usage, capabilities, UUID); ubiquity keys (`isUbiquitousItem`, downloading status, `ubiquitousItemIsDownloading` / `…IsUploaded` …) from isim's local iCloud (below); `setResourceValues` renames (`name`), sets the modification / access dates, and keeps `creationDate`, `isHidden`, `isExcludedFromBackup` (no backups: remembered only), `ubiquitousItemIsExcludedFromSync` and `fileProtection` (not enforced) in a per-device metadata store (`<isim data>/Library/.isim-file-metadata.plist`) that FileManager moves and removals follow; `setTemporaryResourceValue`, `removeCachedResourceValue(forKey:)` / `removeAllCachedResourceValues`.
